biography.plain_text: Roger Milad is a Canadian restaurateur and founder of the Friendship Food Company. He moved from managing A&W restaurants into franchise ownership, building a network across British Columbia's Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island. He later established Milad Brands to hold restaurant businesses alongside investments in property, digital media and travel technology.

long_biography.plain_text:
Restaurateur Roger Milad made a vacant Port Moody pub available for a youth gathering place while the property awaited redevelopment. Dave Jonsson led its conversion into the Belong Centre, with volunteers and sponsors installing skateboarding ramps and an upstairs arcade. The temporary use gave young people an indoor space to skate, meet and stage creative activities.

Through the Friendship Food Company, Milad's family also supported Covenant House Vancouver with monthly donations. That sustained funding contributed to the charity's crisis accommodation for young people experiencing homelessness, as well as meals, clean clothing and employment support.

Identity remains secure through the explicit Friendship role and personal profile; replacement contains only independently attributed Milad facts. Exact historical Sea Axis title was not independently established.

Four wealth fields were independently tested. Current sector is explicitly an origin fallback because the broader portfolio is not economically weighted. Restaurant ownership and continuing founder involvement are positively established despite that ranking gap; no demand for an exact valuation is used to erase that core.

Birth date, birthplace, secondary nationality and expanded middle name remain unverified. A securities source uses middle initial E, while an aggregator supplies an age; neither warrants an expanded name or back-calculated exact birth year. No Canadian birthplace claim is newly proposed.

All seven personal link types were checked: Instagram, LinkedIn, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter/X, Youtube and TikTok. Existing LinkedIn is retained without duplication. No other authenticated individual account was found; TikTok access is restricted. Company websites and charity articles are not personal websites. No matching Wikipedia or Forbes profile was found.

The original Covenant House 2020 article returned 403. The newer recipient letter was independently viewed in full and provides the needed donation evidence; its private beneficiary composite is unused. The company-hosted reproduction is identified transparently.

Only Quick-service restaurants is assigned from the active catalogue. Other restaurant labels overlap, while newer property/media/travel activities lack a separate demonstrated defining scale. Philanthropic participation alone does not require a tag.
